names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 2 Μαΐου, «Άγιος Boris - Μιχαήλ ο πρίγκιπας, Ισαπόστολος και Φωτιστής», with the rank words and the epithets left off. The page prints the first name in Latin letters, Boris, and glosses only the baptismal Μιχαήλ.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 2. мај ст. ст., „Свети Михаил (Борис), цар Бугарски.“ Свети is no rank; „цар Бугарски“ is the rank and the people, which this corpus puts in `types` and in the English display name, and it is stripped. **The bracketed Борис is kept, because it is his second name and not a rank** — the name he was born with, which the body gives as „Борис се покрсти... На крштењу добије име Михаил“ — and the Russian wave already stores a bracketed second name this way, as `peter-uspensky`'s «Петр (Успенский)». Keeping it is also what holds this folder **out** of the bare «Михаил» that `michael-of-chernigov` and `michael-of-klops` share, which was measured and not assumed.

death.note: The Охридски пролог for 2. мај ст. ст.: „...и пресели се у небески живот 2. маја 906. године.“ — 906, and the day, where saint.gr has «Ο Άγιος Βόρις-Μιχαήλ κοιμήθηκε με ειρήνη το 907 μ.Χ.» and heads him «(; - 907)». Two sources one year apart; neither was chosen and the interval carries both. `node .tmp/dd.mjs "906 or 907"` reads it in both packs. No year of birth is printed on either page.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026).
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 2ας Μαΐου — «Άγιος Boris - Μιχαήλ ο πρίγκιπας, Ισαπόστολος και Φωτιστής»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 2 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. He is the tsar of Bulgaria baptised Michael at the end of 864 or the beginning of 865 by the bishop Joseph, abdicated in 888, recalled to depose his son Vladimir, dead 907. **He is not the Boris of the two Russian passion-bearers**: the corpus's `gleb-prince-and-passion-bearer` and his brother died in 1015, and the same 2 Μαΐου listing carries the translation of their relics separately, at `/2072/`, which sends their life to 24 Ιουλίου — two different entries on one day. Nor is he `boris-bogolepov`, a martyr of 1937. **`related` goes only to Photius of Constantinople**, whom the page names as having sent catechists to Bulgaria at Michael's request and as having answered the doctrinal questions put to him; the uncle «Άγιος Μποϋάν (τιμάται 28 Μαρτίου)» who prophesied his missionary work, the monk Theodore Kouphara who first sowed the Gospel in him, his sister, and his sons Vladimir and Symeon have no folders. **`types` follows the listing's own words**: Ισαπόστολος is equal-to-the-apostles, πρίγκιπας prince, and the page has him enter a monastery twice; Φωτιστής, enlightener, has no slug in the corpus's closed vocabulary and none was added. It prints no hymn and names no relic.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 15.05.2026 (2. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети Михаил (Борис), цар Бугарски.“

attestations.note: **The day is Julian 2 May, the same menologion day the Greek keeps him on, and this is the first account of him read for this folder that is not saint.gr's.** **A death widened and neither reading chosen**: „пресели се у небески живот 2. маја 906. године“ against saint.gr's «κοιμήθηκε με ειρήνη το 907 μ.Χ.» and its heading «(; - 907)», so `death` is now 906–907 and reads „906 or 907“; this book also gives the **day**, 2 May, which saint.gr does not. **A rank the two books disagree about was NOT written.** This heading calls him „цар Бугарски“, which BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §5 maps to `king`, where this folder holds `prince` from the Greek reading; `honorific.js` would compose a different word to the reader out of the change, and a conflicting rank is not the missing rank that `types_add` is for. **So `types` was left exactly as it was and the disagreement is recorded here for the author** — reversible in one commit either way. New to the corpus from this page: that he was baptised **under the influence of his uncle and his sister**, where saint.gr credits the captive sister and the monk Theodore Kouphara and has the uncle only prophesy; that the patriarch's priests baptised **the whole Bulgarian people by degrees**; that **many magnates opposed the new faith** and were overcome, and that the cross then shone on the many churches he raised; that he **girded a sword and put his own son off the throne** before returning to the habit, where saint.gr has him seize and punish him; and the book's own closing words for his end, „у благој вери, у правом исповедању Господа нашега Исуса Христа, велик, чесан и благоверан“. **Three names on this page were deliberately left out of the life, and one of them is an open identity.** The Prologue names the uncle **Бојан** — this corpus holds `boyan-enravota`, the Bulgarian prince-martyr, and whether he is this man's стриц is a reading nobody here has made, so **no `related` row was written and the question goes to the author**. It names „светих Кирила и Методија“ and the Петочисленици Охридски, the Five of Ohrid, as those who established the faith among the Bulgarians **and among the Serbs**, preaching in the people's own Slavonic tongue; that sentence is about the mission and not about this man's story, so the names are furniture by BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §6 and are not in the appended paragraph, and no `related` row was written for `clement-of-ohrid`, `naum-of-ohrid` or either brother. Photius, who is already in this folder's `related` and already linked in its life, is named and linked as before. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
